item.title: A note on the A.C. spectrum of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.19416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that limit-periodic Jacobi matrices in the weak exponential class $EC(\eta)$ have purely absolutely continuous spectral type when $\eta$ is sufficiently large, depending only on the $R$-boundedness constant. The proof first establishes homogeneity of the spectrum from the weak exponential approximation rate. A closure theorem for reflectionless Jacobi matrices then transfers reflectionlessness from the periodic approximants to the limit, and a theorem of Poltoratski and Remling rules out singular spectrum on a homogeneous set.
item.dc:creator: Moises Gomez Solis

item.title: New Qualitative and Quantitative Estimates for Neumann Eigenvalues toward P\'olya's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.19455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Enhanced Neumann P\'olya inequality, which is stronger than P\'olya's conjecture, and verify it for many classes of domains, including strip-tiling domains, Euclidean balls, thin product domains, and certain higher-dimensional tiling domains. We develop a geometric removal approach for the Enhanced Neumann P\'olya inequality. In particular, our results provide new classes of domains satisfying the Neumann part of P\'olya's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xiang He, Renjin Jiang, Fanghua Lin, Zuoqin Wang

item.title: Quantitative P\'olya inequalities for annular sectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.19461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove explicit positive corrections to the Dirichlet and Neumann P\'olya inequalities at every positive eigenvalue index of every annular sector. The coefficients depend only on the radii and are uniform in the aperture. Real-order angular integration preserves the exact area term, while directional rounding estimates and radial trials control all frequencies. Optimized bounds attain the sharp circular-arc coefficient for the continuous count. We identify the full sector perimeter asymptotic and a low-index obstruction to using its coefficient throughout the spectrum. The strict Neumann inequality also passes to products with bounded Lipschitz domains.
item.dc:creator: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun

item.title: A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.20097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that Payne's conjecture on the comparison between Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues and buckling eigenvalues does not hold on flat and hyperbolic cylindrical surfaces and on (round) hemispheres.
item.dc:creator: Davide Buoso, Vladimir Lotoreichik

item.title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
item.description: arXiv:2610.19195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Zhongkai Tao, Mengxuan Yang

item.title: New graph invariants based on $p$-Laplacian eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2310.08189v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present monotonicity inequalities for certain functions involving eigenvalues of $p$-Laplacians on signed graphs with respect to $p$. Inspired by such monotonicity, we propose new spectrum-based graph invariants, called (variational) cut-off adjacency eigenvalues, that are relevant to certain eigenvector-dependent nonlinear eigenvalue problem. Using these invariants, we obtain new lower bounds for the $p$-Laplacian variational eigenvalues, essentially giving the state-of-the-art spectral asymptotics for these eigenvalues. Moreover, based on such invariants, we establish two inertia bounds regarding the cardinalities of a maximum independent set and a minimum edge cover, respectively. The first inertia bound enhances the classical Cvetkovi\'c bound, and the second one implies that the $k$-th $p$-Laplacian variational eigenvalue is of the order $2^p$ as $p$ tends to infinity whenever $k$ is larger than the cardinality of a minimum edge cover of the underlying graph. We further discover an interesting connection between graph $p$-Laplacian eigenvalues and tensor eigenvalues and discuss applications of our invariants to spectral problems of tensors.
item.dc:creator: Chuanyuan Ge, Shiping Liu, Dong Zhang

item.title: Flexibility of eigenvalues for graph Laplacians arising from genus 3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.26308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is known that the small eigenvalues of the Laplacian of a Riemann surface close to the boundary of the modular space can be well approximated by the eigenvalues of the discrete Laplacian on a certain graph coming from the pair of pants decomposition of the surface. In this paper, we provide a complete description of the sets of eigenvalues of the weighted graph Laplacian for all graphs on four vertices that correspond to a valid pair of pants decomposition of a surface of genus 3.
item.dc:creator: Alena Erchenko, Dmitry Jakobson, Allison Tsypin

item.title: Sharp Neumann eigenvalue means on triangles
item.description: arXiv:2609.38953v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove two conjectures of Laugesen and Siudeja: the equilateral triangle uniquely maximizes the harmonic mean of the first two positive Neumann eigenvalues at fixed perimeter and their geometric mean at fixed area. The proof uses the two equilateral eigenfunctions and four projected polynomial corrections. Triangle symmetry reduces the associated variational matrices to two-by-two operations and two scalar invariants. Angular comparison and horizontal trial functions then yield the global inequalities. The same argument gives explicit quadratic stability bounds in terms of normalized side-length asymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun
